"BPCL’s commitment to skill development commendable" - Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary at SDI Kochi
articles.full_content:
Kochi, 19 September 2026: “BPCL’s decade-long commitment to skill development through SDI Kochi is commendable. What impressed me most is the focus on inclusive skilling and industry-aligned, future-ready training that truly empowers our youth,”* said Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India, during his visit to Skill Development Institute (SDI), Kochi today.
Shri Chaudhary was accompanied by Shri Sujith Kumar, IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship. He was welcomed by Shri Chacko M. Jose, Executive Director (Kochi Refinery) & Director (Refinery), BPCL - Designate, Shri Meganathan, GM (HR), BPCL, Shri Sivakumar G.S., CEO, SDI Kochi, and senior representatives from BPCL and the Central and State skill development ecosystem.
Established in 2016 by Skill Development Society, Kochi, chaired by BPCL, SDI Kochi is a flagship CSR initiative of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited. The institute has certified around 2,100 dipla holders to date, achieving an impressive *98% placement record. SDI Kochi offers a six-month fully residential program at a nominal fee of only Rs. 5,000/-, making quality skill training accessible to youth from economically weaker sections. Courses offered include: Industrial Electrician, Industrial Welder, Electronic Manufacturing, Fitter Fabrication, and Process Instrument Operator – all designed to meet current industry demands. A key highlight of the visit was the Minister’s interaction with hearing-impaired trainees, where he appreciated their confidence and commitment, underlining the importance of inclusive skilling for self-reliance. The Minister lauded the SDI model and called for stronger collaboration between Government, industry and skill institutions to build a skilled and Atmanirbhar Bharat

Unemployment Rate Reduced from 6% to 3.2% Due to Government’s Flagship Schemes: Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan
articles.full_content:
Union Minister of State Dr. L. Murugan Distributes Appointment Letters to 285 Newly Recruited Candidates at 20th Rozgar Mela in Chennai
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated through video conferencing in the 20th Rozgar Mela, organised at 45 locations across the country, and distributed appointment letters to more than 51,000 newly recruited youth.
Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, participated in the Rozgar Mela held at D.G. Vaishnav College, Chennai. He distributed appointment letters to 285 newly recruited candidates selected for various Central Government Ministries, Departments, and organisations, extending his best wishes to youngsters joining key bodies including the Income Tax Department, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Airports Authority of India, Ministry of Defence, Department of Posts, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), and Southern Railway.
Speaking at the event, Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan said that the newly recruited youth entering Government service would play an important role in achieving the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He urged the recruits to view their responsibilities not merely as securing employment, but as an opportunity to serve the nation and contribute to its holistic development.
He stated that an appointment letter is not merely an order of appointment but an opportunity to serve the nation, noting that Government employees function as representatives and the face of the Government while interacting with citizens. He emphasised that honesty, accountability, empathy, and a humane approach towards the public should remain integral to public service.
The Union Minister highlighted that various flagship initiatives of the Government, including Make in India, Start-up India, Stand-up India, and the MUDRA loan scheme, have enabled the youth to emerge as job creators in addition to being job seekers. He stated that the unemployment rate has declined from 6 per cent to 3.2 per cent as a result of various initiatives undertaken by the Government.
Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan pointed out that the number of startups in the country, which stood at around 400 in 2014, has increased to more than 2.5 lakh, noting that a significant number of startup founders are youth below the age of 30.
He also underscored the importance of continuous learning, adoption of new technologies, and regular upgradation of professional skills. He highlighted the growing opportunities for youth in frontier sectors such as space technology and atomic energy, while noting the increasing participation of women across sectors, including space, defence, education, governance, and public administration.
The Union Minister added that more than 12.75 lakh appointment letters have been distributed through Rozgar Melas so far, reflecting the Government’s dedicated emphasis on creating employment opportunities for the youth.
articles.summary: Murugan Distributes Appointment Letters to 285 Newly Recruited Candidates at 20th Rozgar Mela in Chennai Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated through video conferencing in the 20th Rozgar Mela, organised at 45 locations across the country, and distributed appointment letters to more than 51,000 newly recruited youth. Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. Murugan, participated in the Rozgar Mela held at D.G.

The two-day Education Conclave 2026 on “Implementation of NEP 2020: Vision, Challenges & Opportunities for the North Eastern States” concluded here on Saturday with a call for stronger regional cooperation, skill development, research and industry-academia linkages.
articles.full_content:
Tripura Higher Education Minister Kishor Barman, addressing the valedictory session, said the success of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 would depend on effective implementation and tangible improvements in the lives of students, particularly those in remote areas.
He said education should move beyond degree-oriented learning and equip students with skills, critical thinking, creativity, entrepreneurship and adaptability. He called for greater emphasis on internships, apprenticeships, incubation and entrepreneurship programmes to enable students to become job creators.
Barman also proposed greater collaboration among Northeastern states through faculty networks, shared research infrastructure, student mobility and joint research projects. He identified five key areas emerging from the conclave—access, quality, skills, research and innovation, and entrepreneurship.
Additional Secretary, Higher and Technical Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India, Anandrao V. Patel, stressed the need to integrate skills, industry exposure and multidisciplinary education into NEP implementation.
Patel highlighted the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme and said industry-academia collaboration was essential to prepare students for changing workplace requirements. He also called for greater student mobility across the Northeast through multiple entry and exit, credit transfer and the Academic Bank of Credits.
He said achieving the target of 50% Gross Enrolment Ratio by 2035 would require additional infrastructure, teachers and teacher training, along with coordinated efforts by states.
Patel further highlighted online and open-distance learning, multilingual education, virtual laboratories and digital platforms such as SWAYAM and SWAYAM Plus as important tools for expanding access to education.
The conclave resolutions and outcomes were presented by the officer-in-charge of the Documentation Committee. The session, chaired by V. Lovitoly Sema, Additional Secretary, Higher & Technical Education and Director, Higher Education, Government of Nagaland, concluded with a vote of thanks by Tiakaba Amer, Additional Director, Technical Education, followed by the national anthem.

He said education should move beyond degree-oriented learning and equip students with skills, critical thinking, creativity, entrepreneurship and adaptability. He called for greater emphasis on internships, apprenticeships, incubation and entrepreneurship programmes to enable students to become job creators.

PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme
articles.full_content:
Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the State’s Commitment to empower Traditional Artisans 30 Lakh Beneficiaries Registered Under PM Vishwakarma; Around 24.50 Lakh Have Received Basic Skill Training: Union Minister for MSME Jitan Ram Manjhi Empowering Women Entrepreneurs Key to Building Stronger Families, Communities and a Prosperous Viksit Bharat: MoS Shobha Karandlaje Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) celebrated the occasion at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium in Kolkata, West Bengal
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, celebrated the 3 rd Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal. The occasion marked three years of the Scheme’s implementation and highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen the livelihoods, skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of traditional artisans and craftspeople.
West Bengal onboarded for implementation of PM Vishwakarma in May 2026, marking an important step towards extending comprehensive support to the State’s traditional artisans and craftspeople. The celebrations in Kolkata underscored the scheme’s significance in empowering Vishwakarmas through skill training, modern tools, institutional credit and market linkages.
On the occasion of the 3rd Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma, an exhibition showcasing the rich traditional arts and crafts of Vishwakarma artisans, was inaugurated by Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Cabinet Minister, Ministry of MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, Shri Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal and Shri Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME & Textiles, Government West Bengal. The exhibition provided Vishwakarmas of West Bengal, a platform to showcase their traditional craftsmanship and entrepreneurial skills.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal, highlighted the importance of extending skill training and credit support to traditional artisans and craftspeople in the State. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for the transformative vision behind PM Vishwakarma and acknowledged its significant role in strengthening the livelihood of artisans and craftspeople across the country. Outlining the progress of PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal, he stated that more than 7 lakh applications have been received under the scheme. He stated that Government of West Bengal will expedite provisioning of facilitative support to enable Vishwakarmas avail the benefits under the scheme. The Chief Minister also assured coordinated efforts by the State for effective and timely implementation of PM Vishwakarma across West Bengal in association with Ministry of MSME, Government of India. He called upon the concerned State agencies to strengthen outreach and implementation so that the benefits of the scheme reach every eligible artisan and craftspeople.

Progress and preparation for Special Campaign 6.0 by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
articles.full_content:
The Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters is being organized annually since 2021. To sustain the momentum, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) along with its attached, subordinate offices and Autonomous Body recorded significant achievements under the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) during November 2025 – August 2026 monitored monthly through SCDPM portal: The campaign resulted in :
• Review of 5617 files (both physical and e- files)
• Weeding of 467 physical files
• Closure of 4680 e-files
• Conduct of 61 cleanliness campaigns across the country
• Disposal of Public Grievances : 426
• Disposal of Public Grievances Appeals : 65
• Revenue generated by scrap disposal: Rs 34,105/-
• In addition, substantial focus was laid on the disposal of PMO references, Parliamentary assurances and State Government references.
The Government of India has launched Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign will focus on “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste” across field offices. The campaign is being organized in two phases: the Preparatory Phase (15th – 30th September 2026) and the Implementation Phase (2nd – 31st October 2026) which emphasize on institutionalizing Swachhata and minimizing pendency in offices involving identification of pending references from the PMO, VIPs, State Governments and Parliament, assess the volume of redundant materials to be disposed and finalize the procedures for their disposal, identification of effective collection and segregation of e-waste as per guidelines of MoEFCC for target setting for the forthcoming implementation phase, along with strengthening record and space management practices.
Building on the achievements of previous years, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) along with its attached office, subordinate offices including field offices and autonomous body, is fully geared up to roll out the Special Campaign 6.0 and committed to actively participate in Special Campaign 6.0.

MSME-DFO, Guwahati Empowers 90+ PM Vishwakarma Artisans through One-Day Branding & Marketing Awareness Programme
articles.full_content:
A one-day awareness programme on “Branding and Marketing under PM Vishwakarma Scheme” was organized at Goreswar College Seminar Hall, Tamulpur, to enhance the digital commerce, marketing, and export capabilities of local artisans. The event was organized by the MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Guwahati, in cooperation with the District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), Tamulpur.
The inaugural session featured Chief Guest Sh. Maheswar Basumatary, Executive Member, Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC), who encouraged beneficiaries to expand their enterprises by adopting the latest technologies, highlighting the immense potential and sustainability of products from tribal districts. Special Guest Smt. Hemashri Khanikar, ADC, Tamulpur, reflected on the scheme's journey as it completes three years on 17th September 2026, emphasizing its vital role in recognizing 18 traditional trades such as boat makers, carpenters, and sculptors. Dr. Prativa Potowary, Principal, Goreswar College, was also in attendance.
Throughout the day, officials provided comprehensive guidance on enterprise expansion. Sh. D. K. Rabha, Deputy Director, MSME-DFO Guwahati, outlined core scheme benefits including training, toolkits, loans, and export opportunities. Sh. Sumit Kumar Gupta, Assistant Director, detailed the programme's focus on entrepreneurship, AI, and digital commerce. Technical sessions were further enriched by Sh. Samiran Nandi of RSETI, along with Shri Dibyajyoti Das and Sh. Krishna Menon Deka from DICC, who discussed skill development and allied government schemes. Smt. Bandana Rajbongshi of Walmart Vriddhi emphasized the importance of online selling, encouraging artisans to onboard onto platforms like GeM, Flipkart, and Meesho.
The event placed a strong emphasis on practical digital facilitation. Sh. Ranu Kumar Singh conducted a hands-on AI workshop where artisans experienced using tools like ChatGPT for product marketing. With support from India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), 20 Merchant QR Codes were generated for digital transactions. Furthermore, handholding assistance was provided to 25 PM Vishwakarma artisans to complet e their Udyam Registrations.

NSO Conducts AIDIS, SAS and Migration Surveys Across Nagaland
articles.full_content:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India is conducting field work for data collection of three major nationwide household surveys— All India Debt and Investment Survey (AIDIS), Situation Assessment Survey (SAS) of Agricultural Households, and Migration Survey —across Nagaland. The surveys commenced in July 2026 and will continue up to June 2027.
AIDIS aims to assess the household-level financial conditions, credit access and asset distribution which will support better policy formulation in terms of financial inclusion, credit and economic development.
SAS of Agricultural Households aims to assess the livelihood conditions of agricultural households in order to formulate better planning and policies for rural development.
Migration Survey aims to examine the population mobility and labour movement which will provide useful inputs for planning in areas such as employment, housing, transportation, social security, skill development and urban planning .
The NSO (FOD), R.O. PIB Media Delegation Visits India’s First Floating Solar Power Plant at Omkareshwar Reservoir
articles.full_content:
On the final day of a Press Information Bureau (PIB)-organised media tour of Madhya Pradesh, a delegation of journalists from Jammu visited the 88 MW Omkareshwar Floating Solar Plant on the Omkareshwar Reservoir, gaining first-hand insight into the innovative renewable energy project and its operations.
During the visit, Station Head Shri Jitendra Kumar Sahoo briefed the media delegation on the salient features of India’s first floating solar plant and its 88 MW generation capacity. He explained the functioning of the facility and highlighted various aspects of generating solar power through floating photovoltaic technology installed on the reservoir.
Shri Sahoo informed that the Floating Solar Plant holds immense strategic significance in India's renewable energy landscape. “By utilizing the vast surface area of the reservoir, the landmark project eliminates the need for large-scale land acquisition, preserving valuable terrain for agriculture and local development while substantially offsetting carbon dioxide emissions,” he added.
The journalists also visited the control room, where they were apprised of the monitoring and operational systems associated with the plant. The briefing provided the delegation an opportunity to understand the processes involved in monitoring power generation and managing the plant's operations.
Following the briefing and tour of the control room, the delegation visited the power plant site. The journalists interacted with engineers and technical personnel working at the facility, who explained various aspects of the floating solar installation, including the floating photovoltaic panels, power generation systems and other technical components.
The interaction with the engineers gave the journalists a closer understanding of the engineering, technical and operational aspects of the 88 MW floating solar project, as well as the use of the Omkareshwar Reservoir for renewable energy generation.
Later, the delegation visited the revered Omkareshwar Temple, where the journalists paid obeisance and sought blessings. The temple visit provided the delegation an opportunity to experience the religious and cultural significance of Omkareshwar.
The visit to the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Plant and the Omkareshwar Temple marked the culmination of the media delegation's tour of Madhya Pradesh. The visit was part of the media tour aimed at providing journalists an opportunity to witness major development and infrastructure projects in Madhya Pradesh.
